root_cause.text: `l2cap_sock_new_connection_cb()` in the Bluetooth L2CAP socket layer dereferenced `chan->data` as a `struct sock *` without verifying it was non-NULL, unlike the related callbacks, so a missing parent socket pointer could trigger a null-pointer dereference when a new connection callback ran.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!parent) return NULL;` at the start of `l2cap_sock_new_connection_cb()` before `lock_sock(parent);`, and the commit message says to “Add the same NULL guard already present in l2cap_sock_resume_cb() and l2cap_sock_ready_cb(),” confirming the crash was due to the absent NULL check.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null parent check in the L2CAP new-connection callback to prevent a null dereference.
intent_record.what: A null check for `parent` was inserted at the start of `l2cap_sock_new_connection_cb()`, returning `NULL` immediately if `chan->data` is not present before calling `lock_sock(parent)`.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from dereferencing or locking a null parent socket, avoiding a crash or undefined behavior when a new L2CAP connection callback is invoked without valid parent context.

candidates.rationale: This dereferences `chan->data` and treats it as a parent socket pointer without checking whether it is NULL, which is the root cause of the null-pointer dereference in the new-connection callback.
This uses `parent` immediately after assignment from `chan->data`; if `chan->data` is NULL, locking it will trigger a null-pointer dereference.
